title: Settlements: Rural and Urban
summary: What settlements are, factors in choosing a site, rural and urban settlements, settlement shapes and functions, and the hierarchy of settlements.

notes.text: A place where people live, work and interact, ranging from a single farmhouse to a large city.
The actual piece of land on which a settlement is built.
The position of a settlement in relation to its surroundings: rivers, routes, other towns and resources.

notes.caption: Site factors in the past
rows: A reliable spring, river or well for drinking, cooking and farming (a **wet-point** site)
Above the flood level of rivers (a **dry-point** site); easy to build on
For growing crops and grazing animals
A hilltop or river bend that was easy to defend
Nearby wood, stone, clay and thatching grass
Protection from strong winds and cold, e.g. a north-facing slope in the southern hemisphere gets more sun
River crossings (bridging points), passes, natural harbours and crossroads encouraged trade

notes.text: Today, other factors are also important: **jobs**, **transport links**, **services** (schools, hospitals) and mineral resources. Johannesburg grew because of gold, not because of water.

rows: Small; few people; low population density
Few; people travel to towns for shops, hospitals, banks

items: **Nucleated (clustered)**: buildings grouped close together, often around a water source, a crossroads or for defence. Many traditional villages are nucleated.
**Dispersed (scattered)**: buildings spread out over a wide area, as on commercial farms in the Free State.
**Linear**: buildings in a line along a road, river or valley.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: On a topographic map, look at the pattern of black building symbols. Clusters suggest a nucleated village; buildings far apart suggest dispersed farms; a line of buildings along a road suggests a linear settlement.

The **function** of a settlement is its main economic activity or purpose, for example a **mining town** (Rustenburg), a **port** (Durban, Richards Bay), a **holiday resort** (Plettenberg Bay), an **administrative centre** (Pretoria) or a **market town** that serves surrounding farms.

notes.caption: Settlement hierarchy (from smallest to largest)
rows: Shops, banks, high schools, hospital, police station
International airport, head offices, stock exchange

notes.text: Higher-order settlements have more **high-order services** (such as specialist hospitals) and serve a larger area called their **sphere of influence**.
